terms.definition: A defined interface through which software components communicate.
A software program designed to perform one or more functions.
A value supplied to a command, function, or program.
A file or collection of files produced or retained by a software process.
An executable or other machine-readable software file.
Stored data used to avoid repeating an operation, or the act of storing data for that purpose.
A software type that defines data or behavior for its instances.
Software that sends requests to another software component or service.
Instructions or declarations written in a programming language.
An instruction submitted to a program or command-line interface.
A distinct part of a software system.
Settings that control software behavior.
A named software value intended not to change during its defined scope.
Information represented or processed by software.
An organized collection of data managed for software access.
A software package, component, or resource required by another component.
A file-system container for files or other directories.
A defined interface location at which a software service accepts communication.
A set of runtime conditions and configuration in which software operates.
A software condition that indicates an operation did not complete as intended.
A represented occurrence that software can record or process.
One performance of software instructions or a software operation.
A named collection of data stored by a file system.
A named unit of software behavior that can accept input and produce a result.
A value or name used to distinguish one software entity from another.
Software that realizes a defined behavior, interface, or design.
Data supplied to a software operation.
A defined boundary through which software components interact.
A bounded unit of software work submitted for execution.
Reusable software made available for use by other software.
A recorded sequence of software events, or the act of recording such events.
A unit of information passed between software components.
A software operation associated with a type or object.
A named unit that groups related software.
A software entity represented according to a defined type or structure.
Data produced by a software operation.
A distributable or managed unit of software.
A named input defined by a function, command, or interface.
A representation of a location in a file system or software namespace.
A running software instance or the act of applying defined operations to data.
A set of software instructions designed for execution.
A named value associated with a software object or configuration.
A message or operation that asks a software component to perform work or return information.
Information returned in reply to a software request.
The software or execution environment in which a program operates.
A formal definition of the structure or constraints of data.
Software that receives requests and provides a service or resource.
A software capability exposed for use by other software or users.
The represented condition of a software entity at a point in time.
A represented condition used to report software progress or outcome.
A sequence of characters represented as a software value.
A bounded unit of work represented by software.
A defined verification activity, or the act of performing that activity.
A defined set of conditions and expectations used to verify software behavior.
Data represented by a software expression, field, parameter, or variable.
A named software location or binding that refers to a value.
A distinct identified state of software or data.
A software diagnostic that reports a condition that may require attention.
A software component that performs assigned work.
Transform source code into another executable or machine-processable form.
Set software options or parameters for an intended environment or behavior.
Make software available in a target execution environment.
Convert serialized data into an in-memory software representation.
Cause software instructions or an operation to run.
Data made available outside a software boundary, or the act of making it available.
Software or data brought into a software boundary, or the act of bringing it in.
Place and configure software so that it can be used.
Bring software or data into an active processing context.
Analyze structured input according to defined syntax.
Convert a software representation into a form suitable for storage or transfer.
Check software or data against defined requirements or constraints.
Establish through evidence that software or data satisfies a defined condition.
An alternate name that refers to an existing software entity or identity.
An ordered collection of software values addressed by position.
A condition that software or a test requires to be true.
The process of establishing the identity associated with a software request or user.
The process of determining whether an identity has permission to perform an operation.
A defined performance measurement, or the act of measuring software performance against it.
A data value or type with two logical states, true and false.
A temporary region used to hold data during processing or transfer, or the act of holding data there.
A produced software result, or the process that transforms source inputs into that result.
A unit of digital data commonly composed of eight bits.
A command-line interface through which a user or program supplies textual commands.
The ability of software components, versions, or interfaces to operate together as specified.
Software that translates source code into another executable or machine-processable form.
A measurement of how much specified software behavior or code is exercised by tests.
Information used to establish or prove an identity to software.
The conversion of serialized data into an in-memory software representation.
A distinct software-domain object represented with its own identity or state.
A named part of a structured software record, object, or message.
Controlled data or setup used to establish repeatable test conditions.
A reusable software structure that provides conventions and capabilities for building applications or components.
Structured metadata placed before or alongside a software message, file, or protocol payload.
The stable information by which software distinguishes one represented subject or entity from another.
A structure used to locate software data efficiently, or the act of creating or updating such a structure.
A connection or combined behavior between software components or systems.
A structured file or record that declares the contents, identity, configuration, or dependencies of software or data.
Data that describes other software data, artifacts, resources, or entities.
A measured value used to describe software behavior, performance, or operation.
A controlled change that moves software data, schema, configuration, or state from one representation to another.
A named scope used to distinguish software identifiers from otherwise similar identifiers.
Software that analyzes structured input according to defined syntax.
The application data carried by a software message, request, event, or protocol unit.
An authorization rule or grant that allows a software identity to perform an operation.
The retention of software data or state beyond the operation that created it.
A software component designed to extend another application or framework through a defined extension mechanism.
A defined set of rules for communication or interaction between software components.
A structured request for data, or the act of submitting such a request to a software data source.
An ordered collection of pending software work or messages, or the act of adding an item to it.
A structured collection of related named data fields.
A previously working software behavior that becomes incorrect after a change.
An identified software version made available for use, or the act of making it available.
A value or outcome produced by a software operation.
A repeated attempt to perform a software operation, or the act of making that attempt again.
Sensitive software configuration data that must be protected from unauthorized disclosure.
The conversion of a software representation into a form suitable for storage or transfer.
A bounded period of related interaction maintained by software for a client, user, or process.
A sequence of data processed over time, or the act of transferring or processing data as such a sequence.
A structured collection of data organized into rows and fields.
Operational data collected from software for observation and analysis.
A sequence of software execution scheduled within a process.
A configured time limit after which a software operation is treated as incomplete or failed.
A recorded path of software execution or distributed activity, or the act of recording that path.
A bounded set of software operations treated as one unit for consistency or completion.
Retain software data or state beyond the operation that created it.
